title: Azshara
body: Azshara lies on the northeastern shore of Kalimdor, a land of autumn-colored forests running from the Ashenvale border to high cliffs above the Great Sea. It shares its name with Queen Azshara, and long ago it belonged to the Highborne, the night elf nobility who loved arcane magic above all else. Their cities and temples lie broken along the coast. When the Great Sundering tore the world apart, most of the city of Eldarath fell into the Bay of Storms, and the restless spirits of the Highborne still wander what remains. Now Spitelash naga sift the ruins for relics, satyrs camp in the western and northern hills, and followers of the blue dragon Malygos guard the shores of Lake Mennar. Timbermaw furbolgs hold the mountain villages, cliff giants grind through the stone of the land, and blood elves dig for treasure in the north. Only two small camps fly the colors of the great factions: the night elves' Talrendis Point and the Horde's Valormok.

title: Talrendis Point
body: Talrendis Point is a small night elf camp at the western edge of Azshara, where the road from Ashenvale crosses into these haunted woods. Sentinels keep watch over it, the hippogryph master Jarrodenus tends his mounts, and the bowyer Brinna Valanaar offers bows to passing travelers. Its most unusual guest is Loh'atu, a tauren who has sworn to the Earthmother to aid the elves against the satyrs that infest this land. From here he sends the willing northeast, to lay the Highborne spirits of the Shadowsong Shrine to rest and to break the satyrs of the Haldarr clan.

title: Shadowsong Shrine
body: On a ruin-covered hill in western Azshara stands the Shadowsong Shrine, its broken stones haunted by the dead of the Highborne. Apparitions and lichlings drift among the ruins and fall upon anyone who comes near, their craving for arcane magic undimmed by death. At times the ghost of Varo'then walks among them, once captain of Queen Azshara's guard, who served her and the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients and fell in the final battle at the Well of Eternity. The shrine shares its name with the Shadowsong family of the night elves, though no tale records the link. The Sentinels and their tauren ally Loh'atu would see these spirits set free.

title: Haldarr Encampment
body: Northeast of the Shadowsong Shrine, the Haldarr satyrs have made their camp among old ruins on the western edge of Azshara. Satyrs, tricksters and felsworn crowd its ground. To the tauren Loh'atu they are a disfigured and evil aspect of the night elves, a blight upon sacred lands that Cenarius himself once walked, and he has sworn to help the elves purge them. He will not presume to speak for the night elves on every atrocity these demonic creatures have committed, but he knows enough to want them gone. Just to the north lies the Horde camp of Valormok.

title: Valormok
body: Valormok is a small Horde outpost set against the mountains of western Azshara, north of the Haldarr Encampment. It was once a dozen warriors strong, but the blood elf Magus Rimtori, whom Belgrom Rockmaul of Orgrimmar foolishly trusted, has killed them, and every party sent against her since has failed to return. Ag'tor Bloodfist commands what is left and burns for vengeance. Beside him waits Jediga, an orc sent here as a punishment, who has turned exile into a trade in Highborne relics. The wind rider master Kroum keeps the camp linked to the rest of the Horde, and a provisioner and a weaponsmith serve the few who remain.

title: Ruins of Eldarath
body: Eldarath was once a prosperous Highborne city and a strong fortress in central Azshara. The Great Sundering threw most of it into the Bay of Storms, and what remains clings to the cliffs above the water. Today the Spitelash naga claim the ruins. Warriors, screamers, sirens and serpent guards prowl the broken courts, Lady Sesspira among them, searching for the powerful artifacts the Highborne left behind. Among the rubble lie tablets named for four Highborne wizards, and the cursed spirits of the old city still linger there.

title: Temple of Zin-Malor
body: Amid the Ruins of Eldarath rises the Temple of Zin-Malor, the stronghold from which Warlord Krellian rules the Spitelash who hold the ruins. Serpent guards, sirens and myrmidons ring the old temple, and General Fangferror prowls among them. Krellian keeps himself hidden behind his guards and covets a prismatic shell of strange and chaotic power, a prize whose magic Archmage Xylem has sensed from his tower through scrying. Around the naga, lingering ghosts of the Highborne still drift through halls their people built, and sacred Highborne writings lie among the stones.

title: Bear's Head
body: Along the southeastern edge of the Azshara mountains lie the villages of Bear's Head, outposts of the Timbermaw furbolgs whose larger dens stand farther north at Ursolan. Warriors, pathfinders and totemics guard the huts, and like most of their kin in this land they meet outsiders with hostility. High on a cliff above them stands the tower of Archmage Xylem. No path climbs to it: visitors must find his surly servant Sanath Lim-yo, camped below the cliffs north of the fork where the main road meets the Ruins of Eldarath, and be sent up by his spell.

title: Ursolan
body: Ursolan is the heart of the Timbermaw settlements of northern Azshara, which run south through the hills to Bear's Head. Ursa warriors, den watchers and shamans fill its dens, Gatekeeper Rageroar watches the furbolg lands between, and Thunderhead hippogryphs wheel overhead. What has become of these furbolgs is uncertain. The tauren Loh'atu wonders whether the plague of Felwood has touched them or whether they simply defend a once peaceful people. Their shamans keep odd treasures too: thieves who could not open a sealed blue bag belonging to Lord Ravenholdt sold it to a Timbermaw shaman as a holy relic.

title: Lake Mennar
body: Lake Mennar lies among the hills of southern Azshara, and its shores belong to the blue dragonflight. Followers of Malygos stand guard on every side: blue dragonspawn, scalebanes, mageweavers and magelords. Where the blue dragons gather, those who know the land say, arcane magic is never far, and many suspect the dragonkin are protecting something the Highborne left behind. Those who slip past the guardians find the lake itself calm and safe. Farther east, the great blue Azuregos keeps his own watch over the treasures of this coast.

title: The Ruined Reaches
body: Along the southern coast of Azshara, the Ruined Reaches hold the wreck of the Horizon Scout. The ship lay off the coast in search of a safe anchorage when naga struck, barely an hour after sundown, and sent her to the bottom. Captain Vanessa Beltis and the survivors of her crew now shelter by the shore with the ship's passengers, their cargo strewn about them, and the naga have already returned once for whatever they failed to find. Scouts watch the mouth of the valley for the next attack. Nearby, the gnome couple Blimo and Jubie Gadgetspring keep a house on the beach and sell trade and engineering supplies.

title: Ravencrest Monument
body: At the tip of Azshara's southern point, on cliffs above the Great Sea, stand the shattered remains of a colossal night elf statue. Only its legs still rise from the rock; the rest lies broken across the headland or lost beneath the waves. The monument bears the Ravencrest name, though whom it honored is no longer known. The Spitelash have made it one of their strongholds, and naga battlemasters and enchantresses hold it against all comers. The headland cannot be reached from the sea, only from inland across a bridge.

title: Southridge Beach
body: Southridge Beach runs along the southern shore of the Bay of Storms, east of the Ruins of Eldarath. It is Spitelash country: myrmidons and sirens walk the sand, and a naga called Caravan Master Tset moves among them. The naga have learned to recognize the enchanted coral of these waters, rare even here, and have stripped so much of it from the bay that little remains. Makrinni razorclaws and coralshell lurkers crawl along the tide line, and wreckage drifts in on the surf.

title: Bay of Storms
body: The Bay of Storms is the great inlet of eastern Azshara, where much of old Eldarath lies drowned. Storm Bay murlocs, great wavethrashers and coralshell lurkers haunt its shallows, and mammoth sharks cruise deeper water. Its islands hold strange residents. On one, the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes keeps watch with three felhounds at his side. On another, to the southeast, Duke Hydraxis of the Waterlords holds court among his honor guard. In the north lies Hetaera's Clutch, lair of a hydra who calls herself ruler of these waters and preys on the children of the sea giant Arkkoroc, whose sons and servants roam the bay in turn.

title: Temple of Arkkoran
body: On the northeastern shore of the Bay of Storms rises the Temple of Arkkoran, its weathered stones lapped by the surf. Now it is the seat of Lord Arkkoroc, a sea giant whom even the demon hunter Loramus calls a lesser deity. He dwells at the very top of the temple, while the Arkkoran broods of makrura and murlocs, clackers, pincers, muckdwellers and oracles, swarm its lower levels and attack outsiders on sight. Those who come seeking his wisdom must find a way through them, for his minions will stop at nothing to destroy an intruder.

title: The Shattered Strand
body: The Shattered Strand runs along the northern side of the Bay of Storms, a remote shore of surf and broken rock. Spitelash myrmidons and sirens hunt along it, makrinni scrabblers and Arkkoran makrura pick through the shallows, and wavethrashers, powerful amphibious beasts found nowhere but Azshara, haul themselves up onto the sand. On the cliffs above lives the furbolg Ogtinc, who left his tribe to serve the Cenarion Circle. A cave on the strand bears the name of Scalebeard, a great turtle that seldom shows itself to travelers.

title: Thalassian Base Camp
body: In the hills of northern Azshara, the blood elves of Magus Rimtori have pitched the Thalassian Base Camp. Her reclaimers and surveyors comb the land for Highborne treasures and have found a way to grind the magic items they take into a glittering dust unlike anything a common disenchanting yields. Magister Hawkhelm keeps the camp while Rimtori ranges abroad with her bodyguards. On the ridge, arcane crystals stand about a circle beside an ancient Kaldorei tome of summoning, a hint that the expedition seeks more than relics. The elves keep faith with no partner for long, as the Horde and a certain goblin scout have learned.

title: Legash Encampment
body: The Legash Encampment sprawls across the northern heights of Azshara, north of the Thalassian Base Camp and east of Ursolan. It belongs to the Legashi satyrs, rogues and hellcallers among them, and a satyr called Master Feardred stalks its ground. Thunderhead hippogryphs and mosshoof coursers graze the slopes nearby, untroubled by their demonic neighbors. On a hill at the camp's edge a goblin merchant hides from the blood elves who hired him and then tried to kill him; they named him Kim'jael, little rat, and he has not forgiven them.

title: Bitter Reaches
body: The Bitter Reaches form the wild northeast of Azshara, a high country thick with Thunderhead hippogryphs, mistwing chimaerae and oozes. Along its northern edge the cliff giants have pushed out most other life, and among them walks Monnos the Elder, a giant of fearsome strength. Few travelers come here. Farther east, on the coast beyond the reaches, the Tower of Eldara looks out over a surf where wavethrashers, makrinni and Storm Bay murlocs crawl among the rocks.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Bitter_Reaches (northeast Azshara; hippogryphs, oozes, chimaerae; giants on the northern edge)

title: Azuregos
body: Azuregos is a blue dragon of Malygos's flight, trusted to guard some of its most precious things. He keeps to the hills of southern Azshara, where a thriving Highborne civilization once stood, and wants only to study these magic-rich shores and what the Sundering left behind. He declares this place under his protection and its arcane mysteries inviolate, and the fate of the curious, he says, is simply the price of curiosity. So many orcs and humans come at him with sharp sticks that a visitor may well be speaking to his spirit instead. Charged with a shard of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands, he kept it five hundred years, then handed it to a very special minnow.

title: Duke Hydraxis
body: Duke Hydraxis leads the Hydraxian Waterlords, elementals of water who serve Neptulon and hold that their strength lies in their purity. From an island in the Bay of Storms, ringed by his honor guard, he wages war on the lesser elements of air and earth and above all on fire, whose lords hold the Molten Core beneath Blackrock Mountain. Hydraxis does not pretend to understand mortal notions of gratitude, yet he will strike bargains with those who prove useful. To his most trusted allies he gives vials of aqual quintessence, able to quench the fiery runes on the floor of the Molten Core, conduits that feed the Firelords' power.

title: Loramus Thalipedes
body: Loramus Thalipedes is a night elf demon hunter who dwells on a small island in the Bay of Storms, guarded by three great felhounds, Raytaf, Shahiar and Zaman. He sees what others cannot, and calls mortals sighted but sightless, a gift and a curse alike. His knowledge of demons runs deep, above all of Razelikh the Defiler, once the most feared of Lord Kazzak's lieutenants and now master of the Blasted Lands. Loramus laughs at those who would face the demon lord and calls their courage foolhardy, yet he helps them all the same, if only to see one of Razelikh's minions fall.

title: Lord Arkkoroc
body: Lord Arkkoroc is a sea giant who dwells atop the Temple of Arkkoran, and the demon hunter Loramus names him a lesser deity. He speaks of himself as the one, and grants his wisdom only to those who first serve him. His great grievance is Hetaera, a hydra who calls herself ruler of the oceans and preys on his children. To Arkkoroc she is a false god and nothing more, and he wants all three of her heads. Those who bring them he judges worthy of his wisdom, and from such grisly trophies his giant fists can wring a temper fit for weapons against demons.

title: Archmage Xylem
body: Archmage Xylem is a human mage who lives in a tower high on the cliffs of Azshara, reachable only by a spell cast by his servant Sanath Lim-yo, who sneers at every visitor and is civil to no one but his master. Xylem watches over the land for reasons of his own and studies its Highborne relics with a hunger that unsettles those who deal with him; the orc Jediga trusts him less than anyone she knows. He is generous to those who please him, but he has not forgiven the blood elves who killed one of his apprentices, nor the green drake Morphaz, who swallowed another apprentice whole along with a rare arcane shard.

title: Jediga
body: Jediga is an orc of Orgrimmar sent to Valormok as a punishment by Belgrom Rockmaul, and she has made the most of it. Before she left she learned what valuables lay forgotten in Azshara, and now she sends helpers into the Ruins of Eldarath for four tablets named after Highborne wizards. Each has a buyer: Magatha Grimtotem of Thunder Bluff, who hopes the lore of the alchemist Beth'Amara may help the Forsaken; Jes'rimon, a fence in Orgrimmar's Drag who has eyes for Jediga herself; Andron Gant of the Undercity, too fond of drink, buying for mages who study Markri's summonings; and Archmage Xylem, the buyer she trusts least. Those who carry her tablets earn a fair share of the profits.

title: Kim'jael
body: Kim'jael is a goblin merchant camped on a hill near the Legash Encampment, nursing a grudge. Magus Rimtori's blood elves hired him to help scout Azshara for lost treasure, and at the word treasure he signed on, only for his employers to turn on him and try to kill him. Worse, they gave him a name: Kim'jael, which in their tongue means something like little rat. The elves still hold his compass, his scope, his stuffed chicken and his Wizzlegoober. Kim'jael wants them back, and wants to learn why Rimtori was after a rune the naga of Eldarath now hold, so that he can pay the big bullies back in kind.

title: Loh'atu
body: Loh'atu is a tauren who stands with the night elves at Talrendis Point, on the border of Ashenvale. He has sworn an oath to the Earthmother to aid the elves in purging the satyrs, and he hunts those of the Haldarr clan. He has also promised the Sentinels to free the Highborne spirits from their mortal bonds wherever he finds them, for he believes their hunger for the arcane is a harbinger of the Burning Legion. To those who help him he shares what he knows: of Queen Azshara and her ruinous love of magic, of the cursed Highborne, of the human mage in the northern tower, and of the furbolgs grown hostile.

title: Ogtinc
body: Ogtinc is a furbolg hunter who left his tribe to aid the Cenarion Circle, and he lives atop the cliffs northeast of the Ruins of Eldarath. He no longer hunts for himself; fate, he says, has made him a teacher. Seasoned hunters come to him to build a charm of trophies: perfect courser antlers, wavethrasher scales, and at last the tooth of the green drake Morphaz. For the Circle he gathers a salve to heal Felwood, from the glands of mosshoof coursers, which wisely left that sickened forest long ago, the ichor of Eldarath's undead and the blood of Morphaz himself. Every courser slain grieves him, for the beasts are sacred to the Circle.

title: Betrayed
body: Belgrom Rockmaul of Orgrimmar admits his folly: he trusted a blood elf. Magus Rimtori promised him riches and powerful relics from Azshara if he would lend her warriors for protection, and then she slew them all. At Valormok, Ag'tor Bloodfist tells the rest. His camp was a dozen strong and all are dead; Rimtori played Belgrom like a lute, he says, and seduced him besides. Vengeance begins on the bluffs of the northern peninsula among her reclaimers and surveyors. In her camp lies an ancient Kaldorei Tome of Summoning whose diagram matches a circle of crystals on the ground, one bound to Rimtori herself and the others to something far more sinister. Shattering her crystal draws her out. Her head returns to Orgrimmar in a burlap sack, and Belgrom spits on it.

title: The Name of the Beast
body: Those who hunt Razelikh the Defiler come at last to Loramus Thalipedes, who first makes them hear how the demon lord rose and then performs a ritual of enlightenment to learn how his wards may be broken. Only a weapon forged bearing Razelikh's true name can harm him and those under his command. That name is known to Lord Arkkoroc of the Temple of Arkkoran, and he names a price: the three heads of the hydra Hetaera, who slays his children. When they lie before him he crushes the blood from them into a temper and speaks the name, Rakh'likh. Last, the weapons need azsharite, a hard and malleable crystal the cliff giants of southern Azshara leave behind after devouring the stone and ruins of the land. Loramus's felhounds sniff out the hidden deposits, and the tempered crystal is sent to Galvan the Ancient in Stranglethorn Vale for forging.

title: The Waterlords' War
body: Duke Hydraxis offers mortals a place in the Waterlords' war, but only those who show conviction. His first test sends them to the Crystal Vale in Silithus, where servants of air and earth guard items of power for reasons he does not grasp; he wants their stormers and rumblers destroyed. Then come greater foes. High in Blackrock Spire the orcs hold a captive servant of fire, the Pyroguard Emberseer, and Hydraxis asks for its eye. Next he sends his allies into the Molten Core itself, a stronghold of fire that nothing short of an army can enter, and bids them wage a long campaign until they earn the Waterlords' honor. The last task is the hardest: the hands of four captains of the Molten Core, Lucifron, Sulfuron, Gehennas and Shazzrah. For that feat a coffer in the surf beneath his island holds a hero's reward.
